note: Founding years marked 'circa' are approximate in sources. Events are past, sourced facts only; no projections.

link.label: formed from Guadalajara's break-up, 1989
link.text: After Félix Gallardo's April 1989 arrest, his territory was divided: Chapo Guzmán and Palma got Sinaloa/Sonora routes; Juárez went to Aguilar Guajardo (later the Carrillo Fuentes brothers); Tijuana to the Arellano Félix brothers. Siblings, not parent and child.

link.label: formed from Sinaloa's break-up, 2024
link.text: El Mayo Zambada's July 2024 abduction to the US split the Sinaloa Cartel; Guzmán's sons (Chapitos) and Zambada's faction (Mayiza) have been at war since Sept 2024.

link.label: formed from Sinaloa's break-up, 2024
link.text: Zambada's faction, at war with the Chapitos since Sept 2024 after the Sinaloa Cartel split.

link.label: split from Sinaloa network (via Milenio), 2010
link.text: Dual roots: CJNG grew out of the Milenio Cartel (Valencia family, Michoacán/Jalisco), which worked for Sinaloa's Ignacio 'Nacho' Coronel in Jalisco. After Coronel was killed in July 2010, Nemesio Oseguera ('El Mencho') and others formed CJNG.

link.label: split from Gulf Cartel, 2010
link.text: The Zetas, the Gulf Cartel's armed wing, broke away in early 2010 and went to war with it.

link.label: split from Los Zetas, c. 2015
link.text: Cartel del Noreste emerged from the Zetas' Treviño-family faction around 2015 as the Zetas fragmented.

link.label: formed from La Familia's break-up, 2010–11
link.text: After Nazario Moreno's reported death (Dec 2010) La Familia split: one wing became the Knights Templar (2011); the remnant became La Nueva Familia Michoacana, later led by the Hurtado brothers.

link.label: joined the Cárteles Unidos coalition, 2019–20
link.text: Alliance, not a split: Los Viagras (a former self-defence group) joined Juan José Farías's Cartel de Tepalcatepec and other Michoacán groups in the Cárteles Unidos coalition against CJNG in 2019–20. In Aug 2025 the US Treasury reported Los Viagras had allied with CJNG.

link.label: formed from Guadalajara's break-up, 1989
link.text: The Juárez–Nuevo Laredo corridor went to Rafael Aguilar Guajardo when Guadalajara broke up; Amado Carrillo Fuentes, Ernesto Fonseca's nephew, took it over in 1993. Juárez is Sinaloa's sibling and later its rival, never its offshoot.

link.label: formed from Guadalajara's break-up, 1989
link.text: The Arellano Félix brothers received the Tijuana plaza when Félix Gallardo divided his territory from prison.

link.label: formed from AUC's demobilisation, 2006
link.text: Founded in Urabá by mid-level AUC commanders who refused the 2003–06 demobilisation.

link.label: split from FARC, 2016
link.text: Iván Mordisco's 1st Front rejected the peace process in mid-2016; with Gentil Duarte it became the Estado Mayor Central.

link.label: split from FARC's ex-combatants, 2019
link.text: Iván Márquez, a FARC peace negotiator, rearmed in Aug 2019. It is a rival of the EMC, not its offshoot.

link.label: split from Los Choneros, 2020–21
link.text: Pipo's Lobos had been a Choneros substructure; after Rasquiña's murder (Dec 2020) they led the Nueva Generación breakaway coalition.

link.label: split from Los Choneros, 2020–21
link.text: A Durán Ñetas cell rebranded in 2020 as the Choneros' hit squad. After Rasquiña's murder it joined the Lobos-led Nueva Generación, and from 2022 it realigned with the Choneros.

link.label: split from Los Choneros, 2020–21
link.text: Formed in the late 2010s as a Choneros faction. It broke away after Rasquiña's murder and joined Nueva Generación, then re-allied with the Choneros by 2023.
